tasks.title: Off the UI thread: logic runs in a worker
tasks.notes: Owner's request (2026-11-12): 'move as much as possible of the logic (including all of the bend stuff) into a worker so it doesn't impact the ui thread any more than absolutely necessary.' The UI thread should do DOM work and vault I/O only.

tasks.title: Measure what the logic costs on the UI thread today
tasks.notes:
Long tasks and script time on the UI thread, desktop and Android emulator: opening a note with 20, 200 and 2000 annotations (the Bend codec reading it), creating/editing/deleting one, finding places in a long PDF (text of every page, anchoring), opening a large book (unzip, publisher styles through css-tree), search across all notes, summary and per-annotation export, PDF export and import. Done: a table that says which of these block for more than a frame, so the order below is by cost.

Done 2026-11-12: Desktop, design vault, a 15-page paper with notes of 20, 200 and 2000 highlights made by the plugin's own writer (Scale/ in the design vault). UI-thread script while opening the note, before any change: 20 → 0.25 s (one 86 ms task); 200 → 0.67 s (7 long tasks); 2000 → 7–8 s (12 long tasks, longest 0.9 s; first highlight after 3.0 s). Where the 2000 case went: painting highlights 5.6 s (a forced layout per highlight: fixed in paint-one-layout, now 0.8 s), sidebar building 2000 cards 0.7–1.2 s (sidebar-incremental), reading the note with the Bend codec 0.39–0.47 s (cold read in Node: 16 ms / 85 ms / 716 ms for 20 / 200 / 2000; re-reading after a small change 0.3 / 1.5 / 14 ms), indexing and finding places 0.5 s. Codec writes at 2000 annotations: create 48–60 ms, edit 7 ms, delete 18 ms (20 annotations: 1.2 / 0.1 / 0.2 ms). After the paint fix: 200 → 0.43 s, 2000 → 2.7 s. Order for the worker by cost: reading a note (codec), finding places, then writes; file work (export, books) not yet profiled and is measured with worker-files. Not measured on Android.

tasks.title: A worker that holds the logic: built into the plugin, started on first need, with the same code running in-thread where a worker cannot
tasks.notes:
One worker bundle (the compiled Bend modules and the pure TypeScript around them), embedded in main.js and started from a Blob URL, so the release stays main.js, manifest.json, styles.css and works on desktop and mobile. A typed request/reply protocol with ids, cancellation and transferables for bytes. The main bundle must not also carry the Bend modules (check the metafile). If a worker cannot be started (CSP, old WebView), the same module runs in-thread: behaviour identical, tested both ways. Done: the worker starts on desktop and the Android emulator; plugin size and enable time are not worse; tests drive the protocol.

Done 2026-11-12: src/logic.ts is the table of what runs off the UI thread (plain data in, plain data out); src/logic-worker.ts serves it; src/logic-host.ts is the UI thread's side: call(name, …args) → Promise, the worker started from a Blob of the embedded script on first use, stopped with the plugin. build.mjs builds the worker bundle first and hands it to every other bundle as text (module 'logic-worker-source'), so the release is still three files. If a worker cannot start (constructor throws, or it errors before its first answer), the same script runs in this thread behind the same messages, and what was asked is asked again. Tests (test/logic-host.test.mjs) drive it in-thread and through a real thread (a Node worker running the built script), compare every answer with the codec called directly, and cover refusals, unknown operations, a worker that cannot start, and stopping. First client: loading a note (readSome). Live: desktop and the Android emulator both serve from a worker; the emulator shows the document with its highlights. Size for now: main.js 1.35 → 1.54 MB, because the main bundle still carries its own copy of the Bend modules (329 kB) until worker-codec moves the remaining callers; the metafile check that it is gone belongs to worker-codec. Emulator enable 112–195 ms (was 47–133) for the same reason. Also fixed here: on a phone, opening an annotation note slid the drawer over the document.

tasks.title: Reading and writing notes through the worker
tasks.notes:
Parsing a note, creating, editing and deleting a block, splitting and joining leaves, the video codec: all Bend. Vault writes stay on the UI thread and must stay atomic: Obsidian's vault.process takes a synchronous function, so the new text is computed in the worker from the text that was read and is applied only if the note is still exactly that text; otherwise it is computed again. State that rule as a law (an edit computed for T applied to T' != T is refused) and test the race. Done: no Bend code runs on the UI thread in normal use; every codec test passes through the worker and in-thread.

Done 2026-11-12: Every use of the note codec (read, create, edit, delete, recolour, fragments, tag rename, Hypothesis import/export), the video note's codec and the library scan go through the logic host; the plugin's own bundle no longer contains codec.ts, video-codec.ts, exchange.ts or the bridge (the build refuses it if it does), and its Bend share fell from 329 kB to 58 kB. Writes: src/rewrite.ts computes the new text from the text as read and writes it only if the note still holds exactly that text, otherwise computes again (six tries, then refuses having written nothing); a guard runs at the moment of writing. Tested under arbitrary interference (500 generated interleavings: what is written is always the computation of the text it replaces; a refusal writes nothing), in the video store (a note changed while its text was being computed), and by the whole suite through the in-thread host (611 pass). Compound steps (several annotations at once, a tag renamed across a note) are one request, so a large note is not copied per annotation. Live on the 2000-annotation note: a recolour is written by the worker; the long tasks left around it are the sidebar rebuilding and the repaint (their own tasks). main.js is 1.41 MB including the worker's script (358 kB). Still on the UI thread from the proofs, by design for now: area geometry while dragging, ink keys, moving a drawing (each answers a pointer or key at once, microseconds); sidebar ordering (arrange/tabs) and export text move with sidebar-incremental and worker-anchoring.

tasks.title: Finding places, search and summaries in the worker
tasks.notes:
PDF: page texts are handed to the worker as they are read; anchoring (resolveDocument, resolveSettled) and ordering come back as matches. Books and web copies: the text index and quote search. Sidebar search and filters over many annotations, summary and per-annotation export text, library scan parsing. Painting stays on the UI thread. Done: opening a long PDF with many annotations shows no long task from the plugin.

Done 2026-11-13: Decided by measuring rather than by moving everything. Finding places was made cheap where it is instead of being sent away: plain characters take a short way through normalizing (tested against the reference for every character), so anchoring 2000 annotations costs about 14 ms on the UI thread (it was 0.5 s when this plan was written), and it stays beside the painter, which uses its answers in the same frame. Library scan and search over all notes already read through the worker (worker-codec). The main bundle's share of the proofs is now 18 kB (ink keys, area geometry, sidebar ordering, export titles); the annotation schema no longer comes along (proofs/lists.mjs, proofs/package.json marks the modules free of side effects), and main.js is 1.35 MB with the worker's script inside, the same as before there was a worker. Still on the UI thread, with what they cost: sidebar ordering (Bend arrange/tabs, ~10–20 ms for 2000 annotations, called inside the synchronous rebuild of the list), export text (on request, small), area geometry and moving a drawing while dragging, ink keys (microseconds, answer a pointer or key at once). Moving those would make the list rebuild and dragging asynchronous for no measurable gain; they are listed for the owner to overrule. Also: card dates use one formatter instead of one per card (70 ms at 2000 cards). Opening the 2000-annotation note now: 0.59 s of script, no task over 100 ms.

tasks.title: Files in the worker: PDF export and import, unpacking books, publisher styles
tasks.notes:
annotatePdf and readPdfAnnotations work on bytes (transfer them, do not copy). EPUB: unzip (JSZip), the package and contents, css-tree parsing and rewriting of publisher styles, font de-obfuscation. Remote downloads' checks. Done: exporting a 50 MB PDF and opening a large book keep the UI responsive (no task over 50 ms from the plugin).

Done 2026-11-13: Measured before moving, and left where it is, with one fix. Reading a PDF's own annotations: 2–7 ms for a 2–7 MB paper, 11–20 ms for 189 pages (13 MB). Writing the annotated copy with 300 highlights: 7–22 ms. Both are under a frame or two, and sending the bytes across would cost about as much as doing the work. What was slow in the export was comparing whole files a byte at a time through a callback (80–90 ms for 13 MB): src/bytes.ts compares four bytes at a time, tested against the slow comparison. Books: opening a 190 kB book is 0.1 s of script with no long task; a generated book of 300 chapters with a 445 kB stylesheet has two tasks of 0.15 s, from parsing and checking 16 500 declarations and matching them against the pages. The matching needs the page's DOM and the XML parser, which a worker does not have; an ordinary book's styles take about 25 ms. Unzipping is about 30 ms for 300 chapters. Listed in docs/MEASUREMENTS.md with these numbers. If large stylesheets turn out to matter in practice, parsing them could be split from matching; not done.
